aspect: October 2022 - Lufthansa and Austrian suspend Iran flights
description: A body was found in the undercarriage of an Airbus A340 at Frankfurt after it arrived from Tehran as flight LH 601 and had been moved to a hangar. Lufthansa suspended Tehran flights pending clarification and cancelled the next day's service; Austrian Airlines also cancelled Iran flights.

aspect: EXAMPLE - held, marched and put on a replacement aircraft
description: In 2022 Lufthansa held back an aircraft on the Iran route. Passengers, including elderly travellers, were made to walk a long distance to a poor-quality holding facility, waited there, and were eventually flown out on an unscheduled replacement aircraft.
energy_note: The indignity is the point - it is not what happens on other routes.
notes: Account as related; no press report located. The adjacent documented event is the October 2022 suspension in the row above.

aspect: Sanctions ground the domestic fleet too
description: Iranian carriers cannot buy aircraft or certified spare parts, so the domestic and regional fleet is old and unreliable, and foreign carriers are the only dependable option - until they leave.

aspect: Longer routings cost money and visas
description: Without direct flights, routings go via Istanbul, Doha or Dubai - which means transit rules, sometimes transit visas, and for the UAE a visa an Iranian may not get.
Regional conflict has repeatedly closed Iranian airspace at short notice, stranding travellers mid-route with no rebooking path home.
notes: Airspace closures during the June 2025 hostilities are widely reported; specific dates and passenger impact need verification.

description: A Lufthansa 747 diverted to Istanbul and sat for 34 hours. Long diversions on this corridor are common enough to have their own genre of account.

aspect: EXAMPLE - trapped on the aircraft overnight
description: In a separate Lufthansa case, passengers were kept aboard all night after a cancellation because the airport had closed around them.

aspect: EXAMPLE - 45 hours, seniors and infants, no assistance
description: Lufthansa LH754 Frankfurt-Bengaluru diverted to Istanbul and arrived over 45 hours late. Passengers including senior citizens and infants were stranded at Istanbul reportedly without airline assistance, kept on the plane four hours, then left without proper updates. Lufthansa said oxygen cylinders used in a medical emergency had to be replaced and it took longer than expected.
notes: Not an Iran route, but the closest documented match for the pattern of elderly passengers stranded through a Lufthansa diversion.

aspect: SCENARIO - the rebooking that cost more than the ticket
description: Hassan is booked Tehran-Frankfurt-Toronto to meet his grandson. Lufthansa suspends the Tehran route with nine days' notice. The only rerouting is via Istanbul and Doha, 31 hours, and the fare difference is USD 1,150. He is 58 and has never flown more than five hours.
